questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country of Japan was a natural pick for my mandatory exchange in Japanese Studies – there’s no other country with Japanese as its national language, and indeed, there is an abundance of people able to teach the language expertly. The choice of Tokai was due to its geographical proximity to Tokyo, while still remaining solidly in what most locals would call the “Inaka”.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of the info I needed to travel was clearly sent beforehand, and the small bits of doubt that were left were able to be dealt with by the very responsive Study Abroad team at the destination.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At the male dormitory, there weren’t any Japanese people, but foreign students from the previous semesters assisted the workers tasked with keeping the dormitory in introducing students with limited Japanese capability. There were a number of events targeted exchange students, and these were clearly introduced during Japanese class. I suspect you’d be more hard-pressed to find info on these if you’re not taking Japanese lessons at Tokai, although posters do hang throughout campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Just a single dormitory, sorted in male and female.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: None. The local supermarket is 10-20 minutes by foot, and the kitchen is shared, although feels well-equipped by the leftover utensils from previous exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The rooms are rather old, and are potentially twin (two people in one room). I had an issue with mold in the air condition which was never fully resolved, although the unit was cleaned, and I was given cleaner to clean it myself in the future. Aside from this, there’s a curfew from 23:00, and a ban on having anyone visiting anywhere but the first floor of the dormitory. Finally, there were a lot of bugs, ranging from spiders to cockroaches. Rarely in the rooms, but often in the common areas.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing is EXTREMELY cheap. Expect to pay around 5.000 dkk for a semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super easy for the university-part, although the proceedings for moving in and getting your medical insurance take place in Hiratsuka City Center, about 45-60 minutes by bus from the dorm. If everything is smooth, you’ll only have to go there once.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: University-wise it consists of filling out a sheet of questions, but the Japanese government requires you register your address on your Zairyu card, given to you upon immigration. This is a pretty simple process, although it entails a lot of waiting at the City office (Shiyakusho) and should be done from early morning to avoid having to take the trip twice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Previously enrolled students agreed to go, and if everything is terrible, you could ask one of the Resident Advisors to accompany you. In my exchange, there were only RAs present in the female dorm.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got my wanted classes without lottery, and was even able to change classes midway through. A simple system is used, and it’s rather flexible.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much, just make sure you go with some friends to the City office to make it more fun.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Japanese classes were great, but I was a little bit disappointed with the level of some of the other classes. Still, teachers were undoubtedly qualified and their teachings were worth hearing.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was taking Japanese courses for propedeutics and a few supplying classes for Realia 1 in Japanese Studies.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were more online classes, and many were based on a small summary assignment to prove attendance. There’s also a midterm, which isn’t always customary at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Japanese Intensive Course, upper intermediate. International Tourism. International Relations. International Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Japanese courses are phenomenal and the teachers allow each student to expand their abilities immensely. Even if you’re not required to take it, i recommend the language classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn’t expect the train to Tokyo to be as expensive as it was. The price itself isn’t bad, and Odakyu is among the cheaper rail companies, but it’s a long trip, and you’ll end up taking it a lot. Budget extra for transport, despite practically living on campus.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is surprisingly cheap, and rent is super cheap. I couldn’t believe that we got away with living that cheap, but there aren’t many hidden fees, if any. The supermarket near the station, Gourmet City, is surprisingly expensive, the cheaper ones are a fair distance by foot away.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Students could, principally, join any circle they pleased. There was also an abundance of events, such as the Glocal Fes and the Kengakusai.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Glocal Fes was fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go enjoy the local area. Definitely Kamakura, Enoshima, Hakone, etc., but also local places like Ooyama or the local summer festivals.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy, since many of the foreign concepts had been introduced in class. There are obviously many hidden and unsaid mannerism in Japan, but I didn’t feel as much stress from this as I had expected.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the activities, and arrange day trips and hangouts with them. There’s a whole International College, as well as a Scandinavian Studies residing at the campus, so I also recommend joining these activities and taking these as chances to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I thought carrying cash around was a concept I had trouble getting used to. I was also troubled by the curfew and the general attitude towards university students that they are not yet adults.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It’s with every ounce of seriousness that I applaud the Japanese drinking culture. I have had many fun evenings at the local bars, talking to the locals and making friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to join in on the activities and spend time making local friends. Any city is far away, and if you don’t have something to do in your proximity, you will feel lonely. That said, I also recommend travelling. There’s a Shinkansen station close by in Odawara, and Japan changes a lot depending on the prefecture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I have written everything I think is important in the other boxes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making local friends and being able to expand my language ability exponentially by talking to them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The rules of the dormitory.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
